_comment: Batch 05 (Sets 8-9). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason.

RN-S08-02.A: Slow the transfusion to a keep-vein-open rate and recheck the client's vital signs in 15 minutes
RN-S08-02.C: Administer acetaminophen as prescribed and continue the transfusion at the same rate
RN-S08-02.D: Flush the existing blood tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride to clear the line

RN-S08-04.A: Increasing the heparin infusion rate to treat the new deep vein thrombosis in the leg
RN-S08-04.C: Transfusing platelets to bring the platelet count back toward the normal range
RN-S08-04.D: Switching from heparin to enoxaparin subcutaneously every 12 hours

RN-S08-05.A: Increased platelets, shortened PT and aPTT, elevated fibrinogen, and normal D-dimer
RN-S08-05.C: Normal platelets, normal PT and aPTT, normal fibrinogen, and normal D-dimer
RN-S08-05.D: Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit, normal PT, and decreased D-dimer

RN-S08-07.A: Encourage oral fluids and reassess the client's pain and breathing in 4 hours
RN-S08-07.C: Discharge the client home with oral antibiotics and a follow-up clinic visit in about 1 week
RN-S08-07.D: Apply a cold compress to the chest to relieve the pain and reduce the fever

RN-S08-08.A: "Take each dose with a full glass of milk to reduce any stomach upset it may cause."
RN-S08-08.C: "Take it at the same time as an antacid to protect your stomach lining."
RN-S08-08.D: "Stop taking it and call your provider if your stools turn dark or black."

RN-S08-09.B: "Eating more red meat, eggs, and dairy foods every day will cure this kind of anemia."
RN-S08-09.C: "I'll take iron pills every day for 3 months, and then I can stop."
RN-S08-09.D: "I only need treatment until my energy improves and the fatigue goes away."

RN-S08-13.A: Hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia, hypercalcemia, and low uric acid
RN-S08-13.C: Hyponatremia with all other electrolytes in the normal range
RN-S08-13.D: Normal electrolytes with an elevated hemoglobin level

RN-S08-14.B: Bilateral ankle edema with no swelling of the face, neck, or arms at all
RN-S08-14.C: Hypotension with warm, flushed extremities and a bounding pulse
RN-S08-14.D: Severe low back pain with new numbness and weakness in both legs

RN-S08-16.A: Put on two pairs of gloves, pick up the implant by hand, and reinsert it into the vagina right away
RN-S08-16.C: Discard it in the red biohazard container in the room and document the event in the chart
RN-S08-16.D: Leave it in the bed linens and continue care, then report it at the end of the shift

RN-S08-17.A: Protamine sulfate given by slow IV injection over 10 minutes
RN-S08-17.C: Increased warfarin dose for each of the next 3 days
RN-S08-17.D: Oral aspirin 81 mg once daily with breakfast

RN-S08-18.A: "I'll need to have INR blood tests every week so my provider can adjust the dose."
RN-S08-18.C: "I need to avoid eating spinach, kale, broccoli, and all other green leafy vegetables."
RN-S08-18.D: "If I forget to take a dose, I can just double my next dose so I stay on track with my schedule."

RN-S09-01.A: A client with an MRSA wound infection on contact precautions in a private room with the door closed
RN-S09-01.C: A client with HIV who is asking about medication refills before being discharged home today
RN-S09-01.D: A client with Clostridioides difficile on contact precautions who is resting comfortably in bed

RN-S09-03.A: Gloves, gown, mask, goggles or face shield
RN-S09-03.C: Mask, gloves, gown, goggles or face shield
RN-S09-03.D: Goggles or face shield, gloves, mask, gown

RN-S09-05.B: Live attenuated varicella vaccine to prevent chickenpox and shingles
RN-S09-05.C: Discontinuation of antiretroviral therapy until the CD4 count improves
RN-S09-05.D: High-dose corticosteroids to reduce inflammation in the lungs

RN-S09-06.A: "I can skip my doses on weekends as long as I feel well, since my viral load is already low."
RN-S09-06.C: "Once my CD4 count is back in the normal range, I can stop taking the medication for good."
RN-S09-06.D: "Missing a few doses here and there won't affect whether the medication keeps working for me over the long run."

RN-S09-08.B: "Take each dose with a glass of grapefruit juice."
RN-S09-08.C: "Expect your urine to turn orange while taking it."
RN-S09-08.D: "Stop the medication once your joint pain feels better."

RN-S09-09.A: Document the food allergies in the medical record and notify the dietary department only
RN-S09-09.C: Arrange a test exposure to latex gloves before surgery to see whether or not the client reacts
RN-S09-09.D: No further action is needed beyond completing the routine preoperative checklist

RN-S09-10.A: "Remove your sleeve and inject it into the muscle of your upper arm, the same place you get a flu shot."
RN-S09-10.C: "Use it only if taking an antihistamine such as diphenhydramine by mouth doesn't relieve your symptoms within 30 minutes."
RN-S09-10.D: "After you use it, you don't need any further medical care if your breathing and swelling improve."

RN-S09-14.A: "Hold a lit match to the tick to burn it off, then wash the area with soap and water."
RN-S09-14.C: "Cover the tick with a thick layer of petroleum jelly and wait for it to back out and fall off on its own."
RN-S09-14.D: "Twist the tick quickly while squeezing its body between your fingers to pull it out."

RN-S09-15.A: A nurse who had chickenpox in childhood and has never had a shingles outbreak
RN-S09-15.C: A nurse who received both doses of the varicella vaccine as a teen
RN-S09-15.D: A nurse who had an episode of shingles on the back last year

RN-S09-16.A: Continue the infusion at the same rate and recheck the client's skin and vital signs in 30 minutes to see if it fades
RN-S09-16.C: Administer epinephrine 0.3 mg IM into the outer thigh and call the rapid response team for anaphylaxis
RN-S09-16.D: Discontinue the vancomycin permanently and document a vancomycin allergy in the client's record

PN-S08-03.A: "Give it mixed with a glass of milk at breakfast so it tastes better to your child."
PN-S08-03.C: "Mix the full dose into the child's bottle of formula so your child takes it without noticing."
PN-S08-03.D: "Stop giving it and call the provider if your child's stools turn dark or black."

PN-S08-04.B: White bread, white rice, plain pasta, saltine crackers, and popcorn
PN-S08-04.C: Milk, cheese, yogurt, cottage cheese, and other dairy products
PN-S08-04.D: Apples, bananas, pears, grapes, and other fresh fruits

PN-S08-06.A: "I'll drink plenty of water every day, even when I'm not thirsty."
PN-S08-06.C: "I'll dress warmly in cold weather and wear gloves and a hat."
PN-S08-06.D: "I'll get my vaccines on time to prevent infections."

PN-S08-09.A: Only after the client vomits for the first time
PN-S08-09.C: At bedtime only, to help the client sleep
PN-S08-09.D: Once the client asks for it during treatment

PN-S08-10.A: Rinsing with an alcohol-based mouthwash after every meal and at bedtime
PN-S08-10.C: Brushing the teeth and gums thoroughly with a firm toothbrush twice a day
PN-S08-10.D: Using lemon glycerin swabs to moisten the mouth every few hours

PN-S08-11.A: "It's only hair, after all. It will grow back once your treatments are over."
PN-S08-11.C: "Not everyone loses their hair with chemotherapy, so please try not to worry about it."
PN-S08-11.D: "You should focus on getting better instead of worrying about your hair."

PN-S08-12.A: No special precautions are needed for urine
PN-S08-12.C: Wear a surgical mask only while emptying it
PN-S08-12.D: Wear sterile gloves while emptying the urinal

PN-S08-13.A: "Use a heating pad on the area at night to soothe the irritated skin."
PN-S08-13.C: "Apply a scented, perfumed lotion to the area every day."
PN-S08-13.D: "Scrub the area with a washcloth to remove dead skin."

PN-S08-14.A: Mild tiredness in the late afternoon that improves after a short rest
PN-S08-14.C: Increased appetite at meals and snacking more between meals
PN-S08-14.D: Dry, flaky skin on the hands and lower legs in winter

PN-S08-16.A: Encourage the child to walk it off and keep moving so the knee does not become stiff
PN-S08-16.C: Give a dose of children's aspirin for the pain and swelling, then recheck the knee in about an hour
PN-S08-16.D: Apply a warm, moist heat pack to the knee for 20 minutes to ease the pain and stiffness

PN-S08-17.A: "Have all of your blood pressures taken on your left arm from now on."
PN-S08-17.C: "Carry heavy grocery bags with your left arm to help it get stronger."
PN-S08-17.D: "Keep your left arm hanging down at your side as much as possible."

PN-S08-19.A: "Screening mammograms aren't needed until you turn 60, unless you have a strong family history."
PN-S08-19.C: "You only need a mammogram if you or your provider feel a new lump during a breast exam, so watch for any changes."
PN-S08-19.D: "Screening mammograms are recommended once every 5 years, starting at age 40, for women at average risk."

PN-S08-20.A: Give opioids only when the client reports that the pain has become severe
PN-S08-20.C: Avoid opioids to prevent the client from developing an addiction
PN-S08-20.D: Give the analgesics only at bedtime so the client can sleep through the night

PN-S08-21.A: Mild itching of the face, arms, and upper chest
PN-S08-21.B: No bowel movement in the past 2 days
PN-S08-21.D: Pain rated 3/10 after the last dose

PN-S08-22.A: Increased appetite with requests for favorite foods at each meal
PN-S08-22.C: Increased urine output with clear, pale urine over the past 24 hours
PN-S08-22.D: Improved alertness and more conversation with family for several days in a row

PN-S08-23.A: "No, she can't hear anything anymore now that she is no longer responding."
PN-S08-23.C: "It doesn't really matter at this point, so please don't worry about what you say to her."
PN-S08-23.D: "She can hear you only if you speak very loudly, right next to her ear."

PN-S09-02.A: Rub the hands together for about 5 seconds, then dry them completely with a clean paper towel
PN-S09-02.C: Apply the product only to the palms of both hands and rub them together until dry
PN-S09-02.D: Rinse the hands with warm running water after rubbing the product over both hands

PN-S09-03.A: When shaking hands with a client and the client's family members during introductions on admission
PN-S09-03.C: Only when caring for clients who have a known infection or a positive culture result
PN-S09-03.D: When charting in the client's medical record on the computer at the nurses' station

PN-S09-05.A: Use the unit's shared stethoscope and wipe it with an alcohol pad afterward
PN-S09-05.C: Wear a gown only when the client is actively coughing or sneezing
PN-S09-05.D: Allow the client to walk in the hallway without restrictions or a gown

PN-S09-07.A: Recap the needle carefully using both hands, then carry it down the hall to the sharps container
PN-S09-07.C: Place it on the bedside table to dispose of later, after charting the injection
PN-S09-07.D: Bend the needle against a hard surface before disposal so that it cannot be reused

PN-S09-08.A: Report the exposure to the supervisor right away
PN-S09-08.C: Rub the eyes with a clean tissue to remove the blood
PN-S09-08.D: Complete an incident report about the exposure

PN-S09-09.A: Keeping the client's door open to improve air circulation
PN-S09-09.C: Wearing a surgical mask at all times on the unit
PN-S09-09.D: Giving antibiotics to all clients on admission

PN-S09-11.A: "The shingles vaccine is only recommended for people over 80, so you don't need it yet."
PN-S09-11.C: "You don't need the shingles vaccine if you've already had chickenpox as a child."
PN-S09-11.D: "The shingles vaccine is a single lifetime dose that is given to all adults when they turn 65."

PN-S09-12.A: "Because of your egg allergy, you can never receive any type of flu vaccine, even an egg-free one."
PN-S09-12.C: "You'll need to be admitted to the hospital overnight for observation after you get the vaccine, just in case."
PN-S09-12.D: "You need an allergy skin test with egg protein first, before you can get any flu vaccine."

PN-S09-13.A: "I'll take the doses at evenly spaced times each day."
PN-S09-13.C: "I'll report any severe or watery diarrhea right away."
PN-S09-13.D: "I'll let my provider know if I break out in a rash."

PN-S09-16.A: Use latex gloves for care as long as they are powder-free
PN-S09-16.C: Wear latex gloves over nonlatex gloves for extra protection
PN-S09-16.D: Ask the client to sign a waiver before using latex gloves

PN-S09-17.A: "I'll inject it into the outer side of my thigh, even through my pants."
PN-S09-17.C: "I'll call 911 right after I use the auto-injector."
PN-S09-17.D: "I'll carry it with me at all times, even at home."

PN-S09-19.C: A normal finding for the tongue

PN-S09-20.A: "Spend some time in the sun each day to help improve your skin rash."
PN-S09-20.C: "Avoid all exercise and stay in bed or a chair as much as possible."
PN-S09-20.D: "You can stop taking your medications once your rash starts to improve."

PN-S09-21.A: "Shave the child's head completely so that the lice and nits have nowhere left to live."
PN-S09-21.C: "Keep the child home from school for 1 month so the lice don't spread to other students."
PN-S09-21.D: "Have all of the siblings share the same comb so that everyone in the family gets treated at the same time."

PN-S09-22.A: "Don't say that. You're going to be just fine, and you'll feel better soon."
PN-S09-22.C: "You should have been more careful to protect yourself from getting this infection."
PN-S09-22.D: "Lots of people have HIV these days, so it's really not such a big deal."

PN-S09-23.A: Swab the purulent drainage on the old dressing before discarding it
PN-S09-23.C: Swab the intact skin around the outer edges of the wound in a circular motion
PN-S09-23.D: Apply antibiotic ointment to the wound before collecting the specimen
